column1: # The rule table (plan-vector K5; fidelity's VF1): every feature the renders draw, as a record of how the engine
# reproduces it. One record per line, tab-separated:
#   feature   what it is, and where the plan treats it (D-sections)
#   stage     where its rule runs: P data (the packer, through the port), T world geometry (the core's workers, per
#             tile), S the sun (the workers, per sun bucket), F the camera (the render thread per item, the GPU per
#             primitive and per pixel), M the moment (the app's Kotlin port, about once a minute: the theme block);
#   selectors the per-camera choices that decide whether and how it is drawn (distances, sizes, moments, flags)
#   primitive G1's primitive model (FACE, SEG, JOIN, ELL, TILE, TRI, STENCIL) and the engine's own classes (TEXT glyph
#             runs, SPRITE, GROUP a group's opacity, blend or filter, FILTER a filter's definition, GRADIENT,
#             SCREEN a layer fixed to the screen, RASTER, CAMERA the projection, NONE draws nothing itself); joined by +
#   class     exactness (D10): E0 bit-exact by construction, E1 the same rule in float within a level, E2 the same
#             geometry through another rasteriser within G1's calibration, E3 approximated (D11), X outside the map
#             (eye level, an option the app does not use, an app overlay); several joined by /
#   package   the work package that builds it (plan-vector section 5), - for none
#   source    the renderer's lines it stands for: file:first-last,... (render/), several files separated by spaces
# check_rules.py check holds the table to the renderer's features: every SVG-emitting line, every call of a helper that
# makes markup for its caller, every rule that draws nothing itself (the sun's position, the theme, the light) and
# shade.py must lie in a record's source lines, and every record must cover one of them that no other record covers, so
# deleting any record fails the check. Records of class X cover what the map's cameras never reach. The reachable lines
# and the helpers' callers are recorded below by check_rules.py record.
